Day 1
From Hotel: 25 min → Jama Masjid
1.Jama Masjid
Shah Jahan’s 1656 mosque has a courtyard for 25,000 worshippers. Foreign visitors pay admission and may enter from 8:00am until sunset; Indian visitors enter free from 11:00am. Tourist access pauses for prayers.

2.Red Fort
The 17th-century Mughal fortress of red sandstone from which India's Prime Minister addresses the nation on Independence Day, a UNESCO World Heritage Site with palaces, pavilions, and a sound-and-light show by night.

1.India Gate

Day 5
From Hotel: 9 min → Purana Qila
1.Purana Qila
The Old Fort, built by Sher Shah Suri after his defeat of Humayun in 1540 and completed under Humayun's own restoration a decade later, its massive stone ramparts enclose the Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque, the octagonal Sher Mandal tower, and a stepped baoli reservoir on a site linked by archaeologists to the ancient city of Indraprastha.
Read more
Purana Qila · ₹300 foreigners · 4.1 · asi.nic.in
Daily 7:00am - 5:00pm
~1.5 hr
Mathura Rd · Pragati Maidan
36 min · 7 min → Nizamuddin Dargah
2.Nizamuddin Dargah
The Sufi shrine of the 14th-century saint Nizamuddin Auliya, its marble courtyard threaded with narrow lanes leading to the tombs of poet Amir Khusrau and Mughal princess Jahanara; qawwali singers perform beside the tomb most evenings, continuing a tradition unbroken for seven centuries.
Read more

~45 min

7 min → Safdarjung Tomb
3.Safdarjung Tomb
The last significant garden tomb of the Mughal era, built in 1754 for the statesman Safdarjung in a charbagh layout modeled on Humayun's Tomb; sandstone and marble combine on a raised platform surrounded by fountains and water channels, described by one historian as the last flicker of Mughal architecture.

Delhi's second-largest temple complex after Akshardham, a marble compound of interconnected shrines built from 1974 dedicated to the goddess Katyayani, its lattice screens and carved pillars spread across 60 acres on the city's southern edge.

The ivory-white marble mausoleum Shah Jahan built for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, completed after 22 years of construction by thousands of artisans; a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World, its symmetry and inlaid pietra dura work are considered the high point of Mughal architecture.

Local Tastes
Butter Chicken
Delhi's most famous export, invented at Moti Mahal in Daryaganj in the 1950s — tender chicken in a velvety tomato-cream sauce, best eaten with naan. The original restaurant still operates on Netaji Subhash Marg near Daryaganj.
Moti Mahal · Daryaganj
Chaat
Street snacks built on contrasting layers — golgappa, aloo tikki, and papdi chaat. Chandni Chowk has the oldest chaat vendors in the city; the narrow lanes around Paranthe Wali Gali are the most concentrated stretch.
Chandni Chowk · Old Delhi
Kulfi
Dense, slow-frozen Indian ice cream in flavours of pistachio, saffron, and rose — richer and less airy than Western ice cream; sold on sticks or in clay cups throughout Old Delhi and Connaught Place.
Old Delhi · Chandni Chowk area
Nihari
A slow-cooked meat stew — beef or mutton — simmered overnight with whole spices, eaten for breakfast in Old Delhi; Karim's near Jama Masjid has served it since 1913 and remains the city's best-known address for it.
Karim's · Jama Masjid
Food Delivery
Swiggy
Foreign number: not accepted. — Swiggy requires an Indian mobile number; the sign-up form does not accept international country codes.
Delhi's leading food delivery platform with the widest restaurant network — Old Delhi kebab kitchens to Connaught Place chains. Delivery windows run 30-45 minutes; coverage extends across the full NCR region.
swiggy.com
Zomato
Foreign number: not accepted. — Zomato requires an Indian mobile number; international numbers are rejected at sign-up.
Matches Swiggy's Delhi coverage and often runs steeper discounts; doubles as Delhi's most comprehensive restaurant discovery tool with photos, ratings, and menus. Delivery fees and offers depend on the order and membership terms.
zomato.com

Getting Around
Uber
Foreign number: accepted. — Use the country-code selector and a number that can receive the verification code.
Uber covers all of Delhi and the NCR region. UberAuto and UberMoto cost a fraction of standard cars for short hops; surge pricing is common during evening peak hours and monsoon rains.
uber.com
Ola
Foreign number: accepted. — The form offers international country codes; verify your number before relying on the app.
Ola is Uber's main rival in India and is often cheaper, with broader coverage in outer Delhi neighbourhoods. The app includes auto-rickshaws, bike taxis, and a cash payment option — useful if you prefer not to link a foreign card.
olacabs.com

Heads Up
Akshardham — Security and last entry
Store phones and cameras in the free cloakroom. Last entry is 6:30pm for the evening show; the complex closes on Mondays.
Worth Knowing

Start early — the best Delhi is before 9am

Every major monument is quieter and better-lit in the first hour after opening. The Qutb Minar complex and Humayun's Tomb are nearly empty before 8am; by 10am both can be crowded with school groups. The November-January smog period sees air quality drop sharply — an N95 mask is worth packing if your visit falls in that window.

The Delhi Metro covers most of this itinerary cheaply. The Yellow Line runs through Rajiv Chowk · Connaught Place · to Chawri Bazar for Old Delhi. A stored-value Metro card costs ₹100 deposit and rides are ₹10-60 depending on distance.

Remove shoes at every mosque, gurudwara, and many temples before entering; carry a small bag or use the free shoe racks provided. Jama Masjid and Bangla Sahib provide free head coverings at the entrance — head covering is required for women at both. Akshardham enforces a strict dress code: shorts, sleeveless tops, and short skirts are not permitted; sarongs are sold at the entrance if your clothing does not meet the requirements.
